source: AFP; Africans Press; BBC News; Eye Radio (South Sudan); National Salvation Front; Radio Tamazuj; Sudans Post; The City Review (South Sudan); VOA
notes: On 31 January 2025, armed individuals suspected of being Acholi community members and youth from Pibor (likely members of the Murle community who live in the area) clashed with Bor Dinka cattle keepers at Aru junction in Nyolo Boma of Magwi County (location coded to Magwi, the Magwi County headquarters, in Eastern Equatoria State). Around 41 fatalities (one source reported at least 63 fatalities) and 65 injuries were incurred, while at least 100 people were reported missing and several others displaced. At least 10,000 cattle were stolen. The cattle keepers were ambushed as they were moving their cattle after local authorities recently issued an order for them to vacate the area following increased conflict with locals. The locals alleged that the cattle keepers were herding their cattle in local farms and harassing residents, leading to the displacement of civilians. Security forces had been deployed to investigate and calm the situation while the herders were tracking the stolen animals, which were driven towards Magwi Town. A Bor Dinka community leader accused other militias, including NAS of being involved in the incident against their cattle keepers. NAS, Pibor and Eastern Equatoria authorities denied the involvement of their members. A group of parliamentarians representing Eastern Equatoria State noted that the attacks occurred between 31 January and 2 February 2025 and affected Aru, Amee, Obama, Nyolo, Ayii, Jok Okii, Chomboro, Lowoi, Agoro, and Lofiriha areas in Magwi and Torit counties (further information unknown/not reported).
